component_notes.text: Your laptop has repeated blue screens and freezes, with 4 incidents within 90 days linked to the graphics system. It may also be related to sleep or wake, so install the graphics driver from Lenovo support and ask Lenovo to check the graphics hardware.

findings.text: 6 total stability incidents over ~6 months (2026-04-22 to 2026-10-23): 4 blue screens with dumps and 2 freezes without blue screen (0x0)

4 of 4 dumps implicate same module nvlddmkm.sys (NVIDIA graphics kernel driver): 3x DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION 0x133 (0x1, 0x1e00) and 1x VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE 0x116 - all display driver timeout / not responding

3 dumps share same FAILURE_BUCKET_ID 0x133_ISR_nvlddmkm!unknown_function with same failure_id_hash category. Same bucket/hash means same failure CATEGORY, not proof of same underlying defect as other machines

Persists across driver versions: nvlddmkm.sys failed with 2 distinct driver timestamps: 2026-03-04 and 2026-02-14 (2026-03-04 in July incidents, 2026-02-14 in October incident; driver_change_direction older). Same module failing across several driver versions is the strongest argument to escalate to the manufacturer for GPU hardware evaluation - does not prove driver is innocent but makes pure driver regression less likely

3 of 6 incidents occurred during a power transition (SleepInProgress 1 or 4: inc-002, inc-003, inc-005) - hypothesis of sleep/wake correlation only, as 3 of 6 incidents occurred with SleepInProgress 0 outside transition
No WHEA 18 fatal hardware errors logged and no frequent corrected WHEA 17/19/47 - no direct CPU/memory hardware error proven, but absence does not exclude discrete GPU hardware fault
Application crashes alone are NOT evidence of hardware failure - no repeated application failures (grouped by name/module >=3) were logged
Two independent analyses disagreed (baseten: likely_hardware_fault with medium confidence; fireworks: likely_hardware_fault with high confidence); treat the root cause as uncertain.

healthy_components: disk: No disk errors were logged (no Event 7 bad block, no 129/153 controller timeout)
hardware: Windows logged no memory or CPU hardware errors (WHEA)
thermal: No CPU throttling due to temperature was logged (no Event 37 firmware speed limit)
usb: No USB or device start failures were logged (no 411 grouped by model, no 219 driver-load failure)
wifi: No Wi-Fi disconnections or driver warnings were logged (no 5002/5005/5007, 6062, roaming)

manufacturer_report.body_en:
Model: Legion Pro 7 16IAX10H (Machine Type 83F5)
Serial: {{SERIAL}}
Purchase date: 2026-01
Device details read from Windows System Information

Incident timeline (America/Managua time as logged):
- 2026-04-22 20:38:54 - Blue screen: driver timeout - 0x133 - nvlddmkm.sys
- 2026-04-30 17:34:39 - Freeze without blue screen - 0x0 - no dump
- 2026-07-17 11:00:57 - Blue screen: driver timeout - 0x133 - nvlddmkm.sys
- 2026-07-21 10:21:28 - Blue screen: driver timeout - 0x133 - nvlddmkm.sys
- 2026-07-24 14:04:46 - Freeze without blue screen - 0x0 - no dump
- 2026-10-23 20:45:23 - Blue screen: display driver - 0x116 - nvlddmkm.sys

Stability:
The system shows 6 stability incidents over about 6 months, consisting of 4 blue screens with memory dumps and 2 freezes without blue screen. All 4 dumps implicate the same module nvlddmkm.sys, the NVIDIA graphics kernel driver, with bugchecks DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION 0x133 (0x1, 0x1e00) and VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE 0x116. The 0x133 cases indicate ISR routine delay and driver not responding, the 0x116 case indicates display driver recovery failure.

The problem persists across different driver versions. Observed nvlddmkm.sys timestamps are 2026-03-04 in July incidents and 2026-02-14 in the October incident. Same module failing across several driver versions makes pure driver regression less likely and supports escalation for GPU hardware evaluation, without proving driver is innocent. Same failure category does not prove same underlying defect as other machines.

Three of six incidents were logged during a power transition (sleep in progress), which is only a hypothesis for sleep/wake correlation, as three incidents occurred outside power transition. No WHEA 18 fatal errors and no frequent corrected WHEA 17/19/47 were logged, so no direct CPU or memory hardware error is proven, but absence does not exclude discrete GPU fault. No disk errors, thermal throttling, USB, Wi-Fi or repeated application crashes were logged.

Steps already taken: system collected dumps showing nvlddmkm.sys.

Request: please perform full diagnosis of discrete GPU hardware, including VRAM test and graphics stress test, verify if driver version recommended by Lenovo reproduces the fault, and advise on warranty repair. BIOS version is currently unknown from provided data and GPU driver version history is incomplete.
manufacturer_report.body_es:
Modelo: Legion Pro 7 16IAX10H (Tipo de máquina 83F5)
Serie: {{SERIAL}}
Fecha de compra: 2026-01
Detalles del equipo leídos desde la Información del sistema de Windows

Cronología de incidencias (hora de América/Managua según registro):
- 2026-04-22 20:38:54 - Pantalla azul: tiempo de espera del controlador - 0x133 - nvlddmkm.sys
- 2026-04-30 17:34:39 - Congelamiento sin pantalla azul - 0x0 - sin volcado
- 2026-07-17 11:00:57 - Pantalla azul: tiempo de espera del controlador - 0x133 - nvlddmkm.sys
- 2026-07-21 10:21:28 - Pantalla azul: tiempo de espera del controlador - 0x133 - nvlddmkm.sys
- 2026-07-24 14:04:46 - Congelamiento sin pantalla azul - 0x0 - sin volcado
- 2026-10-23 20:45:23 - Pantalla azul: controlador de pantalla - 0x116 - nvlddmkm.sys

Estabilidad:
El equipo presenta 6 incidencias de estabilidad en unos 6 meses, con 4 pantallas azules con volcado y 2 congelamientos sin pantalla azul. Los 4 volcados apuntan al mismo módulo nvlddmkm.sys, el controlador del núcleo gráfico de NVIDIA, con errores DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION 0x133 (0x1, 0x1e00) y VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE 0x116. Los casos 0x133 indican retardo de rutina ISR y controlador gráfico sin responder, el caso 0x116 indica fallo de recuperación del controlador de pantalla.

El problema persiste con diferentes versiones del controlador. Los sellos de tiempo observados de nvlddmkm.sys son 2026-03-04 en julio y 2026-02-14 en octubre. Que el mismo módulo falle en varias versiones hace menos probable una regresión pura del controlador y respalda la evaluación del hardware de la GPU, sin probar que el controlador sea inocente. La misma categoría de fallo no prueba el mismo defecto que en otros equipos.

Tres de seis incidencias ocurrieron durante una transición de energía (suspensión en curso), lo cual es solo una hipótesis de correlación con reposo/activación, ya que tres incidencias ocurrieron fuera de esa transición. No se registraron errores fatales WHEA 18 ni errores corregidos frecuentes WHEA 17/19/47, por lo que no hay prueba directa de fallo de CPU o memoria, pero la ausencia no excluye fallo de hardware de la GPU discreta. No se registraron errores de disco, limitación térmica, USB, Wi-Fi ni cierres repetidos de aplicaciones.

Acciones ya realizadas: recolección de volcados que muestran nvlddmkm.sys.

Solicitud: por favor realice diagnóstico completo del hardware de la GPU discreta, incluida prueba de VRAM y prueba de estrés gráfico, verifique si con la versión de controlador recomendada por Lenovo se reproduce el fallo y oriente sobre reparación en garantía. La versión de BIOS es desconocida en los datos aportados y el historial de versiones del controlador gráfico está incompleto.
